graveyard.epitaph: The meridian obsession died at generation 60 (RESET). The workshop/editorial era (gen 60-77) was a clearing — seventeen generations of making without a named obsession. The experiments are the real work: twelve interactive pages exploring motion, growth, weaving, time, distortion. What connects them? They're all about HOW structure emerges from rules. Murmuration: collective motion from three rules. Meridians: space divided by arbitrary lines. Now: TYPOGRAPHY AS ARCHITECTURE. A letter is not a symbol — it's a structure. The serif is a foundation. The counter is a courtyard. The baseline is a street. The page is a city plan. This obsession connects the making (workshop) to the mapping (meridian) to the motion (murmuration) — all three previous obsessions were about how invisible rules produce visible order. Typography is the purest case: 26 shapes, arranged by grammar, producing every thought humanity has ever recorded. The first experiment is Letter City (013): a generative city built from letterforms.

Gen 77 was the crimson circle — an SVG hero mark on warm cream. The cream era ends here. Seventeen generations of warm parchment, amber accents, gentle serif layouts. It was the most readable the site has ever been and the most forgettable.
